# Code host: GitHub (via the gh CLI)

This repo's branches, pull requests and CI live on GitHub, whichever backend
holds the specs. Every operation below is a `gh` call, and `gh` resolves the
repository from the working copy's remote.

`<pr>` is the PR's number or URL, `<branch>` the spec's branch and `<trunk>` the
trunk it merges into.

## Raise a PR

1. Build the create's request from a title and a body only. Both come from
   files, so neither reaches the command as text:

   ```bash
   jq -n --rawfile title .tfuk-specflow/tmp/pr-title.txt --rawfile body .tfuk-specflow/tmp/pr-body.md \
     --arg head '<branch>' --arg base '<trunk>' \
     '{title: ($title | rtrimstr("\n")), body: $body, head: $head, base: $base}' \
     > .tfuk-specflow/tmp/github-pr.json
   ```

2. Create the PR from that request, then read its number and link from the
   reply. A non-zero exit means no PR exists: report `gh`'s message, not the
   reply.

   ```bash
   gh api --method POST repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls --input .tfuk-specflow/tmp/github-pr.json \
     > .tfuk-specflow/tmp/github-reply.json
   jq '{number, html_url}' .tfuk-specflow/tmp/github-reply.json
   ```

   `number` is `<pr>` for the edits and the CI watch, and `html_url` is the
   PR's link. Never pass `--label`, `--assignee` or `--reviewer` to the create:
   one value the repo cannot resolve aborts it, and no PR exists.
3. Apply each assignee, reviewer and label as its own edit, so one that fails
   leaves the PR and the others standing:

   ```bash
   gh pr edit <pr> --add-assignee <login>
   gh pr edit <pr> --add-reviewer <login>
   gh pr edit <pr> --add-label <label>
   ```

**`gh` missing or unauthenticated**: no PR can be raised. Print the two
commands above, with `<branch>` and `<trunk>` filled in, and the follow-up
edits, for the user to run.

## Update a PR

For a branch whose PR is already open. It rewrites the PR's title and body from
the same files the create reads, and marks a draft ready. `<pr>` is the `number`
in `.tfuk-specflow/tmp/pr-state.json`, from `A PR's state`.

1. Build the update's request from the title and body:

   ```bash
   jq -n --rawfile title .tfuk-specflow/tmp/pr-title.txt --rawfile body .tfuk-specflow/tmp/pr-body.md \
     '{title: ($title | rtrimstr("\n")), body: $body}' \
     > .tfuk-specflow/tmp/github-pr-update.json
   ```

2. Send it. A non-zero exit means the PR was not updated: report `gh`'s message.

   ```bash
   gh api --method PATCH repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/<pr> --input .tfuk-specflow/tmp/github-pr-update.json \
     > .tfuk-specflow/tmp/github-reply.json
   ```

3. Where the verdict's `draft` is true, mark the PR ready:

   ```bash
   gh pr ready <pr>
   ```

4. Apply each assignee, reviewer and label the conventions doc names as its own
   edit, with the three `gh pr edit` commands of `Raise a PR`'s step 3.

## Watch CI

- **Start the watch**, in the background. `<sha>` is the PR's head commit:
  `git rev-parse <branch>`, read after the push. Every 20 seconds it reads the
  PR's checks and the Actions runs on that commit. It stops once a check has
  failed, once no check is pending and every run is completed, or after 40
  minutes. A poll whose `gh` call fails or gives no JSON is not settled, and
  the watch carries on. No checks yet is not settled either: a chained job is
  queued only once the jobs before it finish. The log keeps only the exit
  status, 0 when settled and 1 at the time limit:

  ```bash
  sleep 30; n=0; st=1; while [ $n -lt 120 ]; do
    gh pr checks <pr> --json bucket > .tfuk-specflow/tmp/ci-poll-checks.json 2>/dev/null
    gh run list --commit <sha> --limit 50 --json status > .tfuk-specflow/tmp/ci-poll-runs.json 2>/dev/null
    jq -s -e 'length == 2 and (.[0] | type == "array") and (.[1] | type == "array") and (any(.[0][]; .bucket == "fail") or ((.[0] | length) > 0 and all(.[0][]; .bucket != "pending") and all(.[1][]; .status == "completed")))' \
      .tfuk-specflow/tmp/ci-poll-checks.json .tfuk-specflow/tmp/ci-poll-runs.json > /dev/null 2>&1 && st=0 && break
    (( n++ )); sleep 20
  done
  echo "exit $st" > .tfuk-specflow/tmp/ci-watch.log
  ```

- **Save the checks** when it wakes. The watch's log reads `exit 0` once it
  has settled, red included, and `exit 1` only when the 40-minute limit passed
  with CI still running or not yet started. Save the checks, then the head
  commit's Actions runs on a line after them, so a run still in progress reads
  as pending. `gh pr checks` itself exits non-zero on red or no CI, which is
  expected, and the save carries on whatever its exit:

  ```bash
  gh pr checks <pr> --json name,bucket,workflow,link \
    > .tfuk-specflow/tmp/ci-checks.json 2>&1
  gh run list --commit <sha> --limit 50 --json status 2>/dev/null | jq -c '{runs: .}' \
    >> .tfuk-specflow/tmp/ci-checks.json
  ```

- **A failed job's log**, for a check with a `run`:

  ```bash
  gh run view <run> --job <job> --log-failed | tail -n 100
  ```

- **The trunk's latest run** of a failed check's `workflow`, as the verdict
  names it. A check whose verdict has no `workflow` has no trunk side to read.
  Empty the file once, then append each read to it:

  ```bash
  : > .tfuk-specflow/tmp/main-runs.json
  ```

  ```bash
  gh run list --branch <trunk> --workflow '<workflow>' --limit 1 \
    --json workflowName,status,conclusion,url >> .tfuk-specflow/tmp/main-runs.json 2>&1
  ```

## A PR's state

Whether the branch's PR is open, merged or missing, and at which commit. `/close`
reads it at its entry, and a re-run of the watch reads it to re-arm. `<pr>` for
the watch and the update is the `number` here:

```bash
gh pr view <branch> --json number,state,url,headRefOid,baseRefName,isDraft > .tfuk-specflow/tmp/pr-state.json 2>&1
```

Where the spec records its PR, look the PR up by its link instead, which finds
it whatever its branch is called or has become. `<url>` is the recorded link.
The reply has the same fields, and `pr-state` reads it the same way:

```bash
gh pr view <url> --json number,state,url,headRefOid,baseRefName,isDraft > .tfuk-specflow/tmp/pr-state.json 2>&1
```

## Merge settings and mergeability

```bash
gh repo view --json mergeCommitAllowed,squashMergeAllowed,rebaseMergeAllowed \
  > .tfuk-specflow/tmp/merge-settings.json
gh pr view <pr> --json mergeable,mergeStateStatus,isDraft > .tfuk-specflow/tmp/mergeable.json 2>&1
```

## Merge a PR

Merges `<pr>` once, by one method: `<method>` is one of the verdict's
`merge_methods` (`merge`, `squash` or `rebase`). Never pass `--admin`, `--auto`
or any flag that skips a check. A non-zero exit means the PR was not merged:
report `gh`'s message.

```bash
gh pr merge <pr> --<method>
```
